item.title: Hendel: I won't be Netanyahu's 61st vote, but I will join a unity government
item.description:
Two days before the polls open, Yoaz Hendel, chairman of the Reservists-Economic Party, addressed his party's standing in the polls and made clear that he would not provide Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu with the 61st Knesset seat needed to form a government. However, he said he would be willing to join a unity government that includes Netanyahu, Naftali Bennett, and Gadi Eisenkot.
"We are the only way to establish a Zionist government without Haredi or Arab parties," Hendel declared, arguing that voting for any other option would lead to another round of elections.

item.description: At Sgt. Yuval Shai Svilem's funeral, Ben-Gvir recalls their personal meeting, invokes Rabbi Akiva, and calls for tougher measures against terrorism.

item.title: Two killed, three injured in serious crash in Beit She’an Valley
item.description: 17-year-old Zohar Tamir of Kibbutz Tirat Zvi, was one of two people killed in a serious car accident in the Beit She’an Valley. Three others were injured and taken to HaEmek Medical Center.

item.title: Bill Ackman: 'Govt. without Ben Gvir, Smotrich would help Israel diplomatically'
item.description: American billionaire Bill Ackman says Ben Gvir and Smotrich have caused enormous damage to Israel's reputation and argues that excluding them from the next government could improve relations with the US.

item.title: IDF eliminates two terrorists who transferred millions to Hamas
item.description: The IDF and ISA say the two terrorists helped funnel millions of shekels from Iran and Turkey to Hamas' military wing. A weapons storage facility in central Gaza was also destroyed.

item.title: The engagement that turned into a nightmare: Another legal victory for the couple
item.description: After the Mount of Olives engagement turned into a terror attack, in a Honenu civil suit settlement, two attackers will pay NIS 26,000 beyond the criminal-case compensation.

item.title: Gun stolen from school security guard in Givat Shmuel
item.description: A suspect snatched a handgun from a security guard at the Kanfei Ruach School in Givat Shmuel and fled the scene. Numerous police officers are searching the area in an attempt to locate him.

item.title: Fearing surprise attack, IDF reinforces troops
item.description: The IDF is reinforcing troops, raising alert levels, and suspending leave. A two-day drill will take place in northern and central Israel.

item.title: Iranian officials: American citizens are considered legitimate targets
item.description:
Two senior Iranian officials, including a senior Revolutionary Guards official, confirmed to The New York Times that Tehran is preparing to harm American diplomats and government officials.
According to the two, Israel and the United States have killed dozens of senior Iranian officials and several members of their families. They claim that as a result, American citizens are also considered "legitimate targets."
